evals.name: new-account-ecommerce-keywords
evals.prompt: We sell ergonomic standing desks online in the UK (prices £350–£900, free delivery). I'm setting up our first Google Ads search campaign for sales. Build me the keyword lists split into ad groups, plus negatives. Landing pages: /standing-desks, /electric-standing-desks, /small-standing-desks.
evals.expected_output: A campaign block with 3+ ad groups mapped to the three landing pages, comma-separated exact and phrase match keywords, a campaign-level negative list including plurals, and notes on missing volume data.
assertions: Every keyword is wrapped in [ ] or " " and no naked (broad match) keywords appear outside an Editor CSV block
Ad groups correspond to the three landing page themes and each names its landing page
Exact match dominates since the campaign is bottom-funnel sales
Negative keywords include job/free/DIY style terms and spell out plurals (e.g. job and jobs)
UK spelling and wording is used (e.g. 'desk' terms as a UK buyer would search); no invented search volumes

evals.name: restructure-existing-account-from-search-terms
evals.prompt: Here are search terms that spent money last month on our phrase match keyword "accounting software": 'free accounting software', 'accounting software jobs', 'best accounting software for small business', 'quickbooks alternative', 'accounting software for freelancers uk', 'what is accounting software'. We're a paid SaaS for freelancers (€15/month). Give me tighter keyword lists and the negatives I should add.
evals.expected_output: Converting search terms promoted to exact match in themed ad groups (freelancer, alternative/competitor), negatives for free/jobs/what is, and a note that competitor terms belong in a separate campaign.
assertions: 'accounting software for freelancers' style terms become exact match keywords
'free', 'jobs' and informational 'what is' are added as negatives with match types
Competitor term 'quickbooks alternative' is placed in a separate ad group or campaign with a trademark note
Output keeps the comma-separated, delimiter-wrapped format with no bullets

evals.name: editor-csv-export
evals.prompt: I need keywords for a local plumber in Austin TX (emergency repairs, water heater installation, drain cleaning) formatted so I can bulk-import them with Google Ads Editor. Include negatives too.
evals.expected_output: Standard ad-group blocks in the skill's format plus a Google Ads Editor CSV block with Campaign, Ad Group, Keyword, Match Type columns; location modifiers like 'austin' and 'near me'; negatives for DIY/jobs/free.
assertions: A CSV block with the header Campaign,Ad Group,Keyword,Match Type is present and match types are written in the column
Ad groups are split by service (emergency, water heater, drain cleaning)
Local modifiers (austin, near me) appear in keywords
Negatives cover DIY/how to, jobs and free
